propositions: Current fixed-threshold cadence (compact.threshold=10) causes retained-snapshot bytes to grow quadratically (Θ(N²)), reaching ~344× amplification at N=8,000 events, because every fold writes the complete state and prior snapshots are never deleted.

Byte/replay-cost-aware trigger (fold when pending_source_bytes ≥ alpha·active_snapshot_bytes) reduces retained-snapshot bytes from Θ(N²) to Θ(N) with tunable amplification ≈1/alpha, while bounding replayed bytes to alpha times the snapshot size.

All three candidate cadence policies (fixed-count, geometric, byte-cost) preserve ADR-0035 contracts—conservative horizon, rebuild-on-stray, crash recovery, mixed-version rollback, and two-clone convergence—because they change only the WHEN trigger, not snapshot placement, source_event_uuids, retire/restore logic, or replay ordering.

Production implementation of byte-cost cadence requires a new config key (compact.snapshot_alpha, default ≤0 for backward compatibility) and must be preceded by an ADR and a dedicated two-clone reconvergence test.
